So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate.

The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.

** Won "Good Practice 2016" the highest award by the leading Slovenian medical publication **
** Named a Top Rheumatoid Arthritis App of 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2019 by Healthline **

RheumaHelper is a mobile rheumatology assistant. It provides a complete toolbox of disease activity calculators and classification criteria the informed rheumatologist can reference during day-to-day work. Easy to use and always with you on your mobile phone, RheumaHelper is the perfect tool for rheumatologists.

** Verified content based on published research **

The validity of the content in the application is checked by Prof. Matija Tomšič, M.D., Ph.D., head of the Dept. of Rheumatology, and Žiga Rotar, M.D., rheumatologist at the Dept. of Rheumatology, both at the University Clinical Centre in Ljubljana, Slovenia.

Included classifications:
• Adult Still's disease [Cush]
• Adult Still's disease [Fautrel]
• Adult Still's disease [Yamaguchi]
• Antiphospholipid syndrome
• Arthralgia suspicious for progression to RA [2016 EULAR]
• Autoinflammatory recurrent fevers (clinical classification)
• Axial spondyloarthritis
• Behçet’s Disease (ICBD)
• Fibromyalgia [2016 ACR]
• Gout [2014]
• Gout [2015 ACR/EULAR]
• Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies specification [2017 ACR/EULAR]
• IgG4-related disease [2019 ACR/EULAR]
• Inflammatory Back Pain
• Peripheral spondyloarthritis
• Polymyalgia rheumatica
• Primary Sjögren's Syndrome [2016 ACR/EULAR]
• Psoriatic arthritis [CASPAR]
• Rheumatoid arthritis [2010 ACR/EULAR]
• Systemic lupus erythematosus [2019 EULAR/ACR]
• Systemic lupus erythematosus [ACR]
• Systemic lupus erythematosus [SLICC]
• Systemic sclerosis [ACR/EULAR]

Included disease activity calculators:
• ASDAS (Ankylosing spondylitis disease activity score)
• BASDAI (Bath ankylosing spondylitis disease activity score
• BVAS (Birmingham vasculitis activity score) [version 3]
• CDAI / SDAI (Clinical / simplified disease activity index)
• DAPSA (Disease activity in psoriatic arthritis)
• DAPSA28 (Disease activity index for psoriatic arthritis 28)
• DAS28 (Disease activity score 28 for RA)
• ESSDAI (EULAR Sjögren’s Syndrome Disease Activity Index)
• ESSPRI (EULAR Sjögren’s Syndrome Patient Reported Index)
• Five-Factor Score
• PASI (Psoriasis area and severity index)
• SLEDAI – SELENA modification (SLE disease activity index)
• VDI (Vasculitis damage index)

All of the included classifications and disease activity calculators are based on referenced equations. All references available inside the app.
